sentences.text: Tianyuraptor was a short-armed dromaeosaurid dinosaur closely related to birds.
The holotype specimen, STM1–3, is a nearly complete skeleton missing only the very tip of the tail.
This individual is estimated to have reached a total length of 1.8 meters.
Its forelimbs were unusually short, measuring only 53% of the length of its hindlimbs.
The tail was relatively long, measuring 960 mm and nearly 4.8 times the length of the femur.
Unlike many other theropods from the Jehol Group, the Tianyuraptor holotype preserves no soft tissues.
Fossils of Tianyuraptor were discovered in western Liaoning, China, within the Dawangzhangzi Bed.
The type specimen of Tianyuraptor was formally described in 2009.
The generic name Tianyuraptor combines 'Tianyu', referring to the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature where the holotype is kept, with 'raptor'.
The specific name ostromi honors John Ostrom, a significant contributor to the study of dromaeosaurid fossils.
Researchers believe the type specimen STM1-3 was a subadult, indicated by incomplete skeletal fusion during growth.
The shortened arms, small furcula, and transversely wide coracoid in Tianyuraptor suggest it was not adapted for gliding or aerodynamic flight.
Tianyuraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
A phylogenetic analysis by Zheng et al. places Tianyuraptor as a basal member of the group containing Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
The authors prefer to suggest that Tianyuraptor is considered a short-armed microraptorine.
Tianyuraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 122 million years ago.
The Yixian Formation, where Tianyuraptor fossils were found, dates from approximately 129.7 to 122.1 million years ago.
Tianyuraptor lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
It is debated whether Tianyuraptor is a basal microraptorine or a basal member of the clade containing other Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
It is debated whether Tianyuraptor is a short-armed microraptorine or a basal member of the clade containing all other Laurasian dromaeosaurids except Microraptorinae.
